newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Hindu nationalists demonstrate mass appeal.
newsitem.headline: India's Hindu nationalists demonstrate mass appeal.

text.p: India's main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) demonstrated on Tuesday that it is the party to beat if the country holds mid-term polls later this year.
Hundreds of thousands of BJP supporters took part in a procession to mark the end of a march by leader Lal Krishan Advani, which covered 15,000 km (9,000 miles) across 21 states in 59 days.

Leaders of the rightwing BJP, the single largest group in the lower house of parliament, say they are confident the latest United Front government, which assumed power less than three months ago, will not survive long.

"Their death is imminent...they are breathing their last," Vijay Kumar Malhotra, chief whip of BJP's parliamentary party told Reuters at a welcome rally for Advani near New Delhi's border with the northern state of Haryana.
"The mass contact programme assumes added significance after the latest stroke the government has suffered," he said.

Malhotra was referring to an announcement by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party, a regional partner in the 15-party coalition, that it planned to quit the government. The announcement has rocked the fractious alliance.

Advani's march came to an end at Delhi's historic Red Fort, where independent India's first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru delivered his maiden speech after India won freedom from British colonial rule in 1947.

Thousands of the BJP's saffron and green flags dotted the route into the Indian capital as Advani, seated on a brightly decorated chariot mounted on a truck, and his convoy of thousands of vehicles, ended their journey.
He was welcomed by 10 elephants, 50 horses, 50 camels and thousands of two wheeled scooters as thousands of saffron-clad onlookers and supporters waved at the chariot.
Party leaders said the march would propel them to power.
A similar march Advani led in 1991 coincided with a surge in the BJP's fortunes -- the party grabbed 120 seats in elections that year, up from 86 in the previous parliament.
Last year, the party emerging as the single largest party in inconclusive general elections and briefly formed a government.
The BJP government resigned after only 12 days, when the United Front and its powerful ally, Congress, joined hands against it in a parliamentary confidence vote.
Opinion polls say the BJP, which now controls 193 of the 545 seats in the lower house, would benefit the most from mid-term polls.
Malhotra said: "This government is a cancer patient. Everyone knows that it is about to die, it is only a question of time."
BJP leaders say they are convinced Gujral's centre-left coalition is short-lived and will tumble by the year-end.
"This government was built with an instability factor and that has worsened manyfold now," said party spokeswoman Sushma Swaraj. "It is a matter of days before this government falls."
